title: P50-family auxiliary objective: a pretraining-only future-token-set head (bag-of-words future summary) on ln_f of the trunk's final state, BCE summed over the 107 token types at weight 0.1, on the 191-claude incumbent (handed-off model unchanged, 9,557,760 params; +30/-8 lines)
description: Idea ID: P50-family (pretraining-only auxiliary supervision; the handcrafted bag-of-words form of future-summary prediction, Mahajan et al. 2025): a Linear(384, 107) head, pretraining-only and dropped at handoff with the MTP module, reads ln_f(h_t) at every proof position and predicts as 107 independent sigmoids which token types occur anywhere in the rest of the proof (x_{t+1} .. EOS); its BCE summed over the vocabulary is added at weight 0.1 next to the next-token CE and the t+2 MTP term, and nothing else changes. MTP showed that a look-ahead target helps expert iteration here (+12 when added in 136-fable, -27 when removed in 193-fable); this adds a whole-remaining-proof target (which hypothesis/fact names, rules and connectives the proof will still use), so the handed-off trunk should encode more of a plan at each step, which matters most for the >= 7-line proofs the metric counts.
hypothesis: Pretraining is data-limited, not step-limited: ~4.7 epochs over the same records in 300 s, train CE ~0.05 by the end, and +23% steps bought ~0 three times (148, 186, 193), so extra supervision per position is the lever, as the t+2 MTP term was. The future bag at position t summarizes the entire rest of the proof; its predictable-but-uncertain part (mean bag 17.6 of 107 types on held-out records; punctuation and EOS are near-certain) is which names (hypotheses and earlier have-facts) and which rules/connectives the remaining lines will use, i.e. a plan. Requiring that set to be linearly decodable from ln_f(h_t), the same state the next-token head reads, pushes the trunk to carry plan information at every step; during RL sampling at T 0.8 that should make more of the 32 samples per target coherent multi-line proofs, so expert iteration harvests more long proofs and the >= 7 eval rises. The head is a single linear map on a normalized state (no extra block), so the trunk, not the head, must do the work, and the per-step cost is small (bench ~19.8 vs ~20.8 steps/s). Counter-hypotheses this also tests: (a) capacity competition at the last layer: the bag readout takes directions of ln_f(h) away from next-token prediction (final val CE up by > 0.01 would show it); (b) the bag's size encodes how much proof remains, a length cue that could tie the model to the <= 6-line training lengths and hurt extrapolation (NoPE heads helped by removing such cues); (c) weight too high, as MTP at 0.6 lost 27 (144). Decision rule fixed now: keep only if the 3-seed mean is strictly above 191-claude's 683.67 (this adds code, so no simplicity allowance); otherwise discard. If the other agent keeps a file first, record.py's rule applies.
expected_delta: -20 to +20 vs 191's 683.7 (central +3); keep needs a 3-seed mean > 683.67. Pretraining 4,950-5,350 steps in 300 s per seed (191: 5,362/5,298/5,220; bench 19.8 steps/s after setup vs 191's bench 20.8, so ~3-5% fewer), ~4.5-4.8 epochs; first step at ~30-38 s; final val loss (next-token CE only) 0.080-0.100 (191: 0.092/0.082/0.086); curve bag_loss (BCE summed over 107 types per proof position) falls from ~15-60 in the first curve point to 0.5-4 by 300 s; held-out greedy after pretraining 0.95-0.98 (191: 0.9705/0.972/0.9585); round-4 RL-solved 1,130-1,210 (191: 1189/1160/1142); handoff n_params 9,557,760 exactly; totals 1,650-2,100 s. Falsifiers: a mean below 660, or final val loss above 0.100 on 2+ seeds (the bag term crowds out next-token fitting). Round-1 harvest is not a falsifier (190/191 showed it swings by hundreds without moving the metric).

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 151-claude except width; PeriLNBlock now replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 1280 (same as 151's 4*320)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 191-claude: none in the handed-off model (forward, KV cache, handoff code unchanged; 6 Peri-LN blocks of width 384, 8 heads of 48: 4 ALiBi + 4 NoPE, d_ff 1280, 9,557,760 params). The pretraining-only MTPHead gains `bag`, a Linear(384, 107) (vocab from make_tokenizer('lean_seq')), and mtp_loss adds BAG_WEIGHT * bag to the total; MTPHead is dropped at handoff as before
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760 (unchanged; CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107, and bench_pretrain on an A40 reported the same). Pretraining-only module (never registered on the model, dropped at handoff): 1,916,779 = 191's MTP module 1,875,584 + bag head 41,195 (weight 107x384 + bias 107); pretraining trains 11,474,539 in total; the harness caps the handed-off model (9.56M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the MTP module (with its bag head) is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged code (caches[0] holds key positions); 186's CPU check applies (cached vs full max abs logit diff 1.4e-6)

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices and the new bag head weight (107,384) join Muon, its LayerNorms/biases (incl. the bag bias) join AdamW
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock from step 1, no warmup: lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget (setup and per-block compile included, so the first step runs at ~0.99 x peak after ~30-35 s), ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor. Removed: 186's 200-step linear warmup (lr = 1e-3 * step / 200 for step < 200)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same cosine fraction as AdamW from step 1, no warmup (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices, plus bag.weight (107,384): 31 Muon matrices (191: 30); bag.weight's shape scale is sqrt(384/384) = 1, like head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters (now including the bag head), before both optimizers (unchanged rule)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module (with the bag head) and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2, input proj (384,768) and the bag head weight (107,384): 31 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged (the 200-step warmup those runs had is removed in 191, see optimizer.schedule). The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.compile: per-block torch.compile(dynamic=True), coalesce_tiling_analysis off, undone at handoff; Muon step as one CUDA graph; fused AdamW; batch max length from host
config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384 (this now includes bag.weight); LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0; new: bag.bias constant -2.0 (sigmoid 0.119, near the 17.6/107 = 0.164 mean bag density) so the first steps are not spent on base rates

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp + BAG_WEIGHT * bag with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 and BAG_WEIGHT = 0.1, constant over the whole budget; curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss (mtp_loss) and bag loss (bag_loss)
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]
loss.bag: future-token-set BCE: at each position t with a proof-token target (m[:, 1:]), target y_t in {0,1}^107 with y_t[v] = 1 iff token type v occurs among the proof tokens x_{t+1} .. x_end (EOS included; prompt and pad positions excluded via the proof mask; computed as one_hot(x[:, 1:]) * m[:, 1:], reversed cumulative sum over time, > 0); logits = bag(ln_f(h_t)) with h_t the trunk's final state (the same ln_f output the next-token head reads); per-position BCE-with-logits summed over the 107 types, then mean over proof positions. Local check: targets match a brute-force loop on 6 held-out records; mean bag size 17.6 of 107 at proof positions

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence) on this pretrain.py: 451 steps in 60.3 s, first step at 35 s after setup and per-block compile, 297 steps from 45 to 60 s (~19.8 steps/s; 191's bench 20.8), peak 7.43 GB, n_params 9,557,760, sampling 196 samples/s, dynamo 3 unique graphs; make -C code check clean; CPU smoke (40 s, 1,500 held-out records as stand-in data) ran 4 steps
config.init_rng: not identical to 191 per seed: constructing the bag head (default init, then fork _init) consumes CPU RNG before the orthogonal_ loop, so the trunk's orthogonal draws shift; data order and shift augmentation (CUDA generator and random.Random seeded as before) match 191 seed for seed
